title: Box API: Authentication and Rate Limits (2026 Guide)
summary: Box API includes authentication types, plans, and rate limits for bulk uploads.
body_markdown:
## Calling Box endpoints without code in Activepieces


Without code, Activepieces covers the same ground. A Box connector handles common file, folder and upload actions, and an HTTP step reaches endpoints the connector doesn't, so a failed part gets retried inside the workflow instead of in your script.


Describe the invoice intake in the built-in chat, with the supplier subfolders and the upload step, and it builds and publishes the flow for you, which then runs under the same run traces as any flow you assembled by hand, so each Box call and each 429 is readable afterwards.


The Box connector is one of the 746 integrations counted in the` packages/pieces/community` folder of the open source monorepo, under the MIT-licensed core, so the code behind each Box action is on GitHub to read before you point it at a bulk upload.


Activepieces counts a run as 1 credit however many steps it has, but Box's limits stay exactly where they were: 240 uploads and 1,000 general calls per minute still decide what a bulk upload can do, whatever plan or authentication type you chose earlier.


### Connecting a Box account


You authorize a Box account once, and every step in the flow reuses that connection. Whoever authorizes it decides whose files the flow can see, so connect with the account type you picked on day one, not whichever login is open in your browser.


A flow built on a personal login breaks the week that person leaves.


You set retries on the step, not in code. For the chunked upload described above, put each part in its own step, let a failed step retry on its own, and add the commit step after all parts succeed.


That gives you the retry-then-commit order without a hand-written backoff loop. Retrying faster doesn't beat a rate limit, so check Box's published limits for your plan before you rely on it.


### Using the HTTP step for uncovered endpoints


Of the[150+ endpoints](https://box.com/platform) Box advertises, a connector built for common actions won't wrap all of them. That means anything unusual, such as a niche metadata or admin call, goes through the HTTP step.


There you set the method, URL, headers and body yourself and take on reading Box's docs for that endpoint.


Keep the credential out of the step. The Data Selector below, opened on the Variables tab, lists a single stored value, STRIPE_PROD, next to a Code step's input panel.


A Box token belongs in the same place, referenced by name, so rotating it's one edit rather than a hunt through every step.


Once the credential lives there, the HTTP step and the connector can share it, and the same flow can mix both without anyone pasting a secret into a field.
